Latest Update: 25 Years Later, Dragon Quest’s Island-Hopping Epic Gets Better in Every Port

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (952 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Dragon Quest franchise has been around for longer than some of us have been alive, and its first entry in 1986 was one of the JRPG genre’s pioneers.
  • Recent findings suggest that in North America, Dragon Warrior 7 (the last entry in the series to bear that localized title), arrived after two previous installments weren’t released outside Japan.
  • According to recent reports, dragon Quest 7 spent a long time in development and arrived late enough in the original PlayStation’s life cycle that it felt decidedly old-fashioned by the time any of us got the chance to play it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Dragon Quest franchise has been around for longer than some of us have been alive, and its first entry in 1986 was one of the JRPG genre’s pioneers. Over the years, the launch of a upcoming title in the series has been a big deal, especially in Japan. Before players missed work to play Grand Theft Auto 6, they were using sick days to topple wicked dragonlords.

Recent findings suggest that in North America, Dragon Warrior 7 (the last entry in the series to bear that localized title), arrived after two previous installments weren’t released outside Japan. Interest had waned. When the game hit stores on Nov. 1, 2001, it was as difficult to find as its NES predecessors had been. And when loyal fans finally tracked it down, we wound up being disappointed. But over the years, Square Enix has made some adjustments and tried again on multiple occasions. Happily, each newly introduced release of Dragon Quest 7 gets better than the one before it.

According to recent reports, dragon Quest 7 spent a long time in development and arrived late enough in the original PlayStation’s life cycle that it felt decidedly old-fashioned by the time any of us got the chance to play it. The visuals were a step above anything the Super Nintendo offered, finally rendered in 3D with a camera that players could rotate. But the experience still felt a bit like a step back compared to the flatter but more detailed environments of late PS1-era games like Final Fantasy 9. In some respects, it was a relic from a time many players had moved on from.

It has been revealed that the quest’s opening hours didn’t correct that first impression. I remember playing for three hours without encountering a single enemy mob, which just felt odd. In the typical Dragon Quest game from years prior, you could head outside the castle walls within a few short minutes. An hour into the adventure, you would have already battled dozens or even hundreds of monsters and leveled up your characters several times. Instead, I had to spend that time solving tedious puzzles.

Slow opening hours eventually gave way to a lengthy quest with plenty of appeal, but I didn’t actually stick around to experience those later events until Dragon Quest 7: Fragments of the Forgotten Past launched on the 3DS on Sep. 16, 2016 in the West. Despite making its debut on portable hardware, the new release offered a superior way to experience the adventure.

The single change I appreciated most was an patch to the formerly tedious first few hours of play. The introductory dungeon, with all of its levers and backtracking, was gone. Introductory areas still ate up more time than I was accustomed to, but they fit within a single gaming session and left me with time — and enthusiasm — to progress to more interesting activities.

In a recent development, the 3DS version offered other enhancements, as well. The bottom screen provided a helpful glow when the player approached stone tablet shards, a major component of progression. Players had a lot less guesswork to find essential items, a smart adjustment that eliminated a lot of pointless frustration.

According to recent reports, another fresh feature recapped the story, in case players stepped away for a few days, weeks, or longer. Accessible from the pause menu, a chronological log listed every major event that had occurred, along with hints about where to go next. (Later games in the series, all the way up to Dragon Quest 11, would keep this addition.) While exploring, party members might also offer suggestions if consulted, sparing players from some of the ambiguity that had been a franchise staple since its first installment.

Recent findings suggest that quality-of-life enhancements didn’t stop there, either. The game also introduced enemy mobs players could see in the field as they explored. Leveling up required less grinding, and menus were modified and streamlined. A map on the bottom screen made it easy to spot nearby points of interest. Most importantly, players could make a quick save outside of churches if they needed to stop playing suddenly. For a portable game, that option was a must.

Dragon Quest 7 on the 3DS remained the best way to play the game for a decade, until Dragon Quest 7 Reimagined debuted in February 2026. Available on Switch, Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X, the updated take on the classic adventure introduced a breathtaking upcoming art style. Presented like a diorama, the gorgeous visuals paired nicely with quality voice acting to bring the world’s story to life like never before.

A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

The newest release also introduced fresh changes to the character vocation system, allowing party members to adopt two vocations at once and gain mastery in both of them. Changing a class no longer required a time-consuming visit to Alltrades Abbey, either. And on the world map, striking weaker monsters defeated them automatically with lesser rewards, a welcome compromise that eliminated the need to endure tedious skirmishes. There were other changes, as well, including multiple difficulty presets, a shared inventory, and auto-revive after battle for party members who perished in the fight.

In a recent development, for RPG fans in 2026, these were smart adjustments. Few players appreciate busy work and random encounters that slow the pace more than necessary. It’s good to see developers revisiting past triumphs and modernizing them for contemporary audiences to enjoy. If at first you don’t succeed, try, try again. It certainly worked for Dragon Quest 7.

Guarding Stars Was Adorable, But Can We Talk About That Stalker Twist?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (714 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This year’s Christmas movie releases are in full swing now that it’s mid-November, and I knew I had to check out Guarding Stars with my Netflix subscription.
  • Recent findings suggest that before we get into my lows about Guarding Stars, I have to give the movie its flowers.
  • In a recent development, it’s the kind of movie where we all know they were going to fall in love by the end, but I was instantly curious about how these two were going to fall for each other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This year’s Christmas movie releases are in full swing now that it’s mid-November, and I knew I had to check out Guarding Stars with my Netflix subscription. I mean, it unites Gilmore Girls’ Jared Padalecki with Gossip Girl’s Leighton Meester, so I was in for the 2000s nostalgia alone. I was really digging this lighthearted rom-com (that’s sometimes an action movie), but then that twist just made me go “WTF!” Let’s talk about it. But be warned, there are SPOILERS ahead!

Recent findings suggest that before we get into my lows about Guarding Stars, I have to give the movie its flowers. I’ve seen a lot of holiday rom-coms, and this one had the right amount of sweetness and depth I want from this kind of movie. It follows the fake dating trope pretty much to a T, but I really enjoyed what Padalecki and Meester in particular brought to it as Jack and Hannah.

In a recent development, it’s the kind of movie where we all know they were going to fall in love by the end, but I was instantly curious about how these two were going to fall for each other. I like that they brought out the softness in each other despite both of them being otherwise hardened by their current lives, and I really liked the mother/son dynamic between Jack and Andie Macdowell’s Connie.

Guarding Stars also had that nice balance of goofiness, wit and emotion that I want to see from a Christmas Netflix movie that stopped it from falling into simply being a holiday screensaver. I know it’s based on a popular book called The Bodyguard, and after seeing it I would definitely pick it up, especially to see what changes were made.

However, I thought the Guarding Stars really dropped the ball on the whole “stalker” plotline. Not that I’d expect it to be a huge part of the movie to begin with, but when it was revealed that Nadine was Jack’s stalker near the end, I was so taken aback. It felt way too convenient that one of two people he meets outside of his family and his bodyguard crew ended up being the stalker, and particularly having happened to be in the same place where he was hiding away.

To me, it would have made a lot more sense if the stalker travelled to his location after seeing the kiss cam video with Hannah go viral. Instead, the only information we get is that they knew each other in high school and she divorced her husband to be with him. And then, her husband was somehow vengeful of Jack? The stalker payoff was so unbelievably thin, and felt like a bummer. Especially when the rest of the rom-com put a lot of attention on character development and fun moments for the other characters.

Perhaps the filmmaking team thought the audience wouldn’t care about the plotline not concerning the romance? But, to me, it just cheapened the rest of the viewing experience. I hope more Netflix rom-coms can build out their scripts. If it’s going to be partly an action mystery, I don’t want to feel like no attention was put on that aspect of the movie.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Look, all in all, Guarding Stars had some elements that had me putting it on the nice and naughty list, but overall, I’m happy I checked it out. But come on, Netflix, if you want to shock me, I know you can do better than that.

Who Will Be The Next Bond Girl?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping.
  • It has been revealed that the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux.
  • Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, latest Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

It has been revealed that the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). Her magnetic performance made Madeleine an unforgettable Bond girl, especially since her character plays a decisive role in the arc of Craig’s character: at the end of No Time to Die, the famous spy sacrifices himself to save her and their daughter, Mathilde. For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

In a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she remarked with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”.

Sources indicate that when pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux said. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”.

In a recent development, the online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

It has been revealed that bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”.

Sources indicate that denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”.

Originally published by Vanity Fair France.

Breaking: The Hunger Games' Haymitch Actor Had A Hot Take About Sunrise On The Reaping Making Him Say 'Lenore Dove' Over And Over

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, joseph Zada has had a lot to say about the process it took to become Haymitch in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, so I wasn’t surprised he had more to say.
  • The actor brought the energy while discussing the movie during a BBC Radio 1 interview, and two of his co-stars had to step in to lend a helping (and humorous) hand.
  • I did not want to say 'Lenore Dove.' Didn’t want to say the full name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, joseph Zada has had a lot to say about the process it took to become Haymitch in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, so I wasn’t surprised he had more to say. However, the actor “being completely honest” about something he didn’t like wasn’t on my Bingo card… and this time it’s not about how Zada’s hair is different. The actor shared his hot take about Sunrise on the Reaping making him say ‘Lenore Dove’ over and over, and I have to admit, he has a point.

The actor brought the energy while discussing the movie during a BBC Radio 1 interview, and two of his co-stars had to step in to lend a helping (and humorous) hand. When it came to saying his girlfriend’s name, he didn’t understand why he had to say the full thing:.

I did not want to say 'Lenore Dove.' Didn’t want to say the full name. Didn’t want to say the full name! What are you talking about? Actually, I shouldn’t go that far. But like it’s your girlfriend! That’s why I went to darling a lot. But like you have to say the full–there’s not many people you have to say their full name the whole time.

Industry observers note that while Zada explained, Whitney Peak, who plays Lenore Dove, first chose to stay out of it, saying, “I’m so quiet right now.” Something tells me she’s heard this hot take a few times while filming. The actor shared that he attempted to sneak in a “Lenore,” but director Francis Lawrence wasn’t having it and would correct him. Zada assumes the precise name was a Suzanne Collins choice, which is the second time Peak playfully intervenes by shushing him.

Recent findings suggest that his energy would make fans proud, as I’ve seen plenty of hot takes regarding the book-to-screen adaptations. Those were mostly back in the Peeta vs. Gale days. Thankfully, Zada's other co-star, Mckenna Grace, sweeps in at the last second to clarify his comments:.

I think that the point, before you get yourself in trouble, is that Joe is trying to make, as his media-trained translator, I think that you’re trying to say that because ya’ll have such a close bond, you didn’t wanna feel like you were calling her her full government name the whole time.

Nothing was as enjoyable as watching her and Peak attempt to explain the name to him. Peak suggested it was like saying the name ‘Mary-Anne’ and that Lenore Dove had an invisible hyphen. Fans will also appreciate her giving Lucy Gray a shout-out. However, the actor shared that part of the problem had to do with the accent. He has previously discussed working to nail the dialect, so, understandably, it would trip him up.

Sources indicate that zada assures us that he did become “accustomed” to the name, and that it just “felt unnatural originally” for him to say the “lovely beautiful name.” He's definitely bringing the Haymitch charm to life. This energy is one of the many reasons fan response has been largely positive. This is no small feat, as a lot is riding on this movie given its connection to The Hunger Games trilogy, and knowing we'll be seeing the original actors back. Even author Suzanne Collins was emotional seeing Woody Harrelson come back for the movie.

In a recent development, we'll finally be able to see Zada as Haymitch now that the movie has come to the 2026 schedule this weekend. This also means fans will be able to count how many times Zada says "Lenore Dove." Hopefully, someone will count the number.

Tech Report: Rachael Leigh Cook Plays Twins In Her New Hallmark Movie. I’m Surprised At What Weirded Her Out

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (808 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas lineup this year has been one of the best yet.
  • Acting in general is hard, but having to act opposite yourself while playing co-leads of a movie is even harder (unless you're Lindsey Lohan, who found playing twins easy).
  • I was concerned that there wouldn’t be enough conflict within the movie because I was too far inside it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas lineup this year has been one of the best yet. From reinventing the time-loop wheel to an incredible third season of Mistletoe Murders, it’s been hit after hit, and it doesn't seem to be slowing down. In fact, Thanksgiving week is going to be even bigger with the release of Lacey Chabert’s Disney World movie and Rachael Leigh Cook’s newest film, where she pulls double duty playing twins. I'm excited to see Cook take on the roles, but I'm also surprised over a concern she had.

Acting in general is hard, but having to act opposite yourself while playing co-leads of a movie is even harder (unless you're Lindsey Lohan, who found playing twins easy). Cook is obviously a veteran at this point, so I never would've expected that she would feel apprehensive every time she stepped on set of Double Booked for the Holidays:.

I was concerned that there wouldn’t be enough conflict within the movie because I was too far inside it. I was concerned that just me yapping away at myself was going to be a bad time.

The She’s All That star is set to play identical twins Abigail and Charlie, who end up in Wales for Christmas to help run an AirBnb/bookshop for the week. While there, both women connect with local men: Tom (Owain Yeoman), a barista who works next to the shop, and Lord Rhys (Stephan Hagan), the son of the author behind a popular book series that takes place in the town.

It has been revealed that cook might be concerned about the lack of conflict within the narrative, but I don’t think she has anything to fret about. After all, neither Tom nor Lord Rhys are aware that Abigail and Charlie are twins, which is bound to lead to some hilarious and maybe even tense situations.

Still, the actress couldn’t help but worry when she realized how much screen time she’d be sharing with herself, telling Us Weekly:.

When I started to watch it, my first reaction to seeing myself in stereo was, ‘Oh no, this is way too much. I’m the worst scene partner I’ve ever had. This was a bad idea.’ Because it’s a lot. But then I was able to sort of relax into it and say, ‘OK, I think I was able to differentiate them by enough.’.

Recent findings suggest that differentiating between Abigail and Charlie brought up its own set of complications for Cook, as her characters are identical twins with similar preferences when it comes to their appearance. This is definitely something that hasn’t been done before, since most movies that feature twins give each character something unique to help audiences tell the difference. Thankfully, Cook found other ways to help audiences tell her characters apart — at least she hopes she did:.

It has been revealed that I knew that the worst thing people could feel while watching was confusion. So that was high on my priority list to avoid.

It has been revealed that hallmark movies aren’t known for their confusing nature, so I’m feeling confident about the direction of the film. If anything, it might feel like an immersive experience if viewers can’t tell her characters apart and could allow them to empathize with the men who are falling for Cook's respective characters.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Rachael Leigh Cook might not be considered the “Queen of Hallmark” like Lacey Chabert, but she has become a staple at the cable channel over the years. In fact, this is her second film with Hallmark just this year! Obviously, she’s made a good impression on the network and fans, considering the powers that be trusted her to play dual lead roles in this latest yuletide flick.

On that note, check out Double Booked for the Holidays, which premieres on the Hallmark Channel tonight, November 22nd, at 8 p.m. ET. I know I’ll definitely be tuning in tonight to catch it, and if you can’t watch live, the holiday flick will be available to stream on Hallmark+ the next day.

I can’t believe the release of Sunrise on the Reaping means I’ve been going to the theaters for The Hunger Games movies for nearly fifteen years! I just rewatched the franchise and recalled one gripe I had about the movie when I first saw it that I actually understand now as an adult.

Sources indicate that these days I think the original The Hunger Games movie is pretty great, and I’ve rewatched it so many times. I remember when I went to see it back then, I thought it was a faithful adaptation, but I was bummed that they decided to take out the fact that Peeta loses his leg in The Hunger Games. Check out this excerpt from the end of the first book:.

Caesar asks Peeta how his 'latest leg' is working out. 'New leg?' I say, and I can't help reaching out and pulling up the bottom of Peeta's pants. 'Oh, no,' I whisper,' taking in the metal-and-plastic device that has replaced his flesh.

Recent findings suggest that in the movie, Peeta gets injured like in the book, but Katniss nurses him back to health, and he completely recovers by the end. Yet, in the source material, Peeta is practically bleeding out right before they become the final people in the arena. Katniss is desperate to help him, and she suggests they both have poisonous berries so she can save them both. When they reunite for the post-victory interview with Caesar Flickerman, she learns that his leg had to be amputated right after they left the arena.

Recent findings suggest that I think when The Hunger Games movie came out, I thought the movie was censoring an vital aspect of the story. Peeta’s major injury really had me on the edge of my seat while I was reading the book, so it was sort of anticlimactic for the movie to completely skip it.

However, it just dawned on me during my recent rewatch (with my Hulu subscription) that I haven’t thought about this change to The Hunger Games in a really long time. I guess, ultimately, it didn’t really matter that Peeta only has one leg in the scope of the whole series, and it probably would have caused some extra special effects headaches for the filmmaking team.

In a recent development, there’s something else. Ultimately, I’m realizing that both Peeta and Katniss have so many horrific things happen to them throughout the series that maybe it was OK for the movies to skip Peeta losing a leg. I mean, what happens to Peeta in Mockingjay alone is just heartbreaking. The guy loses his entire family, he’s captured by the Capitol and starved. And then, his brain is altered so he thinks Katniss is his enemy. That’s some really rough stuff.

Now, I think overall The Hunger Games movie series did a great job of adapting the maturity of the book series, but now I’m OK with the films taking out a few extra traumatic things like Peeta’s amputated leg.

The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace‘s 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Press Tour Looks

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances.
  • With the upcoming Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend.
  • In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the upcoming Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Industry observers note that molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and remarked, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to New York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

According to recent reports, right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in Newly introduced York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

My personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Mckenna is a massive fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

She's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

In a recent development, what she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

According to recent reports, mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

He remarked, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she remarked, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

Recent findings suggest that she was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR stated, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

Industry observers note that it makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

The way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had noted that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I remarked, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

What was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me latest references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

What made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

Recent findings suggest that that was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

With the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom noted, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a significant franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has said, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Recent findings suggest that because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a significant fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

According to recent reports, what do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

It has been revealed that I think the major movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

The looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How notable is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

It kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. McKenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

According to recent reports, I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

What is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

It's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

Every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most key part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. McKenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

According to recent reports, will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

Industry observers note that in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the Upcoming York City premiere?

We are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

In the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

According to recent reports, pamela then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Sources indicate that getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

Sources indicate that so when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and noted, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

What's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend noted, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

Well, here we are: the end of the year. The days are shorter, the nights are longer, and our bank accounts are getting smaller. You know why: the holidays are upon us, which means we all have to spend money like the good little consumers we are. The official unofficial launch of the holiday season always begins on Black Friday, that day after Thanksgiving where we wake up hungover from eating too much and start looking for major beautiful deals.

Recent findings suggest that if you're a horror movie fan, I've thrown together a little list of five great Black Friday deals on horror movies, all of which are under $20! That's not bad, especially these days, when everything is outrageously expensive. So if you're a physical media collector and looking for something spooky to drop a few bucks on, keep reading.

Recent findings suggest that danny Boyle's "28 Years Later" returned to the post-apocalyptic franchise he began with "28 Days Later," and he scored a major box office hit in the process. Unfortunately, "28 Years Later" was meant to be the first of a newly introduced trilogy, and the second movie, this year's "28 Years Later: The Bone Temple," wasn't a hit at all. As a result, the fate of the third and final movie in this new franchise is right now uncertain.

In a recent development, which is a damn shame, because "The Bone Temple" absolutely rules. In fact, I think it's better than "28 Years Later." Ralph Fiennes returns as Dr. Ian Kelson, seemingly one of the last good men in a post-apocalyptic landscape overrun by rage-infected zombies and murderous groups of scavengers. This time, Dr. Kelson comes face to face with the deranged Jimmy Crystal (Jack O'Connell), all while trying to find a cure for that pesky rage virus.

"Evil Dead Burn" is the latest entry in the long-running franchise, and it did something no previous "Evil Dead" film did before: it made some fans think the movie was just a little too nasty. The franchise has become known for its over-the-top gore, but Sébastien Vaniček's film is so relentlessly aggressive that it rubbed a lot of fans the wrong way.

According to recent reports, me? I liked it. In fact, I would argue that while the film is definitely unpleasant, Vaniček also tries to inject some humor into the proceedings. It's a very dark and twisted kind of humor, but it's there. In "Evil Dead Burn," recently widowed Alice (Souheila Yacoub) gathers with the family of her dead husband. Unfortunately, the family doesn't really like her, and she doesn't like them either. To make matters worse, the family is soon possessed by those pesky Deadites, and Alice has to fight like hell to survive.

When Tom Cruise was cast as Lestat de Lioncourt, the brat prince at the heart of Anne Rice's "Interview with the Vampire," there was plenty of backlash — including from Rice herself, who thought Cruise was all wrong for the role. Rice eventually admitted she was wrong, however, because you know what? Tom Cruise gives one of the best performances of his career as Lestat, a foppish vampire who just wants to have a good time drinking blood and living his best afterlife.

Sources indicate that if there is a weak link in Neil Jordan's luscious film adaptation, it's Brad Pitt as Lestat's morose vampire companion, Louis. Pitt reportedly didn't have a good time making the movie, and it indicates in his performance. Despite this, "Interview with the Vampire" is a lavish Hollywood horror flick with a lot to offer, including a star-making turn from Kirsten Dunst as Claudia, who is turned into a vampire as a child and is thus trapped in a child's body forever.

It has been revealed that at this point, "Obsession" needs no further introduction. Curry Barker's mega-hit horror flick has a knockout performance from Inde Navarrette as Nikki, the object of affection for her longtime friend Bear (Michael Johnston).

According to recent reports, when Bear gets hold of a magical doodad known as the One Wish Willow, he makes a wish for Nikki to love him more than anyone else in the world. Of course, this wish backfires terribly, and it's made even worse because for all his "nice guy" nonsense, Bear is actually a horrible, selfish creep.

Equal parts funny and scary, "Obsession" got a lot of hype, and I genuinely believe it was worth it: this movie works exceptionally well, and I wouldn't be surprised if Navarrette scores herself an Oscar nom for her work here.

In a recent development, zach Cregger's "Weapons" is yet another highly-hyped horror movie that lives up to its reputation. Borrowing a page or two from "Magnolia," Cregger's film gives us multiple narratives surrounding the mystery of a mass disappearance of children who were all in the same classroom. Their teacher (Julia Garner) becomes a suspect, and one of the missing kid's fathers (Josh Brolin) starts playing detective to true to solve the mystery himself.

Of course, by now everyone knows one of the biggest and best parts of the film is the malevolent Aunt Gladys, played to perfection by Amy Madigan, who earned herself a Best Supporting Actress Oscar for her now-iconic performance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holiday time at Walt Disney World is always one of the best times to visit, but theme park fans might want to postpone their trips to the “Most Magical Place on Earth” until later in 2027. That's when all the newly introduced and upcoming attractions are slated to open, like the new Indiana Jones ride in Animal Kingdom. In case anyone has been wondering, Imagineers have been hard at work on the ride, and they’re finally giving fans a first look at the magic they’re crafting.

It has been revealed that the latest Indiana Jones attraction was unveiled back in September 2025 at Disney’s Destination D23 event in Orlando, Florida. The news was originally met with concern from Disney World enthusiasts. It’s always exciting to see a park get a new ride, especially Animal Kingdom, which right now has the fewest amount of rides out of the four parks. However, the introduction of Indiana Jones meant the loss of the beloved Animal Kingdom attraction Dinosaur.

It has been revealed that time heals most wounds, though, and now that the sting of losing Dinosaur has started to wane, most fans are finally getting excited for the fresh attraction. To further build excitement, Walt Disney Imagineering shared the following clip on its Instagram:.

A post shared by Walt Disney Imagineering & Disney Live Entertainment (@waltdisneyimagineering).

I was definitely not thrilled about the Animal Kingdom changes at first, but I think I’m going to love this fresh version of Indiana Jones! I’m definitely on board with the name that was declared back at D23 earlier this year, and I absolutely love the Mayan-inspired facade. Dare I say it puts the Indiana Jones temple at Disneyland to shame (and hopefully won't have to deal with brawls over line cutting).

I Honestly Never Thought I’d Live To See The Day Disney World Fixed One Broken Attraction.

When the ride eventually opens sometime next year, guests will embark on an adventure alongside Indy that will take them to a temple that legend notes has a water passageway that leads to an underworld protected by a mythic serpent. Imagineers are still keeping much of the actual ride experience under wraps for now. However, with two other cart-style Indiana Jones attractions at other Disney parks and reports that the Dinosaur ride is being rethemed instead of totally demolished, it’s safe to say that this version of Indiana Jones will take guests on a bumpy ride full of twists, turns, snakes (or serpents in this case), and adventure.

Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent will be found in the new Tropical Americas expansion at Disney’s Animal Kingdom. Specifically, the thrill ride will be part of the Bonanche Bioreseve area of the expansion, which is being modeled after the Maya region. This will mark the second Indy attraction to explore Mayan culture, but the first in the United States.

Sources indicate that perhaps the most exciting thing about the latest ride is that real-life Indiana Jones actor Harrison Ford was used as the model for the attraction’s animatronic. While it’s not confirmed whether or not he’ll record lines too, I’m definitely hoping he will. And if he does, then this will definitely be the best Indy ride.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

According to recent reports, there’s still a lot of work to be done on the Indiana Jones ride and the Tropical Americas land, which will include a section dedicated to Encanto. For now, fans can keep the excitement going by streaming the adventure franchise with an active Disney+ subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2002, Drew McWeeny, then writing as Professor Moriarty for the pioneering website Ain't It Cool News, published a script review that got many a cinephile's engine revving. The upstart indie auteur Darren Aronofsky had written an ambitious science fiction screenplay that skillfully bopped between 16th century Mexico, the present day, and the year 2500. But there was a catch: it was an intimate epic about the inescapability of mortality. I read the original screenplay, and my immediate takeaway was that Aronofsky had worked a sorrowful riff on "2001: A Space Odyssey." It wasn't taking on the mysteries of the universe; it was about understanding, on a human and cosmic level, the mystery of grief.

"The Fountain" was greenlit on a $60 million budget with Brad Pitt and Cate Blanchett cast as lovers facing, in the present day, the certain death of the latter via cancer. Pitt's character is a cancer researcher who's unwilling to accept Blanchett's death; he's close to a breakthrough, but the die is cast. When the budget threatened to balloon, Warner Bros. got nervous. Then Pitt dropped out, Blanchett followed and the project was pretty much dead.

Industry observers note that but Aronofsky, much like the protagonist of his screenplay, couldn't let go. He scaled back the screenplay, figured out a way to deliver the eye-popping visual effects at a reasonable cost, and somehow got Hugh Jackman and Rachel Weisz to sign on at a reasonable price. "The Fountain" was greenlit yet again, at which point Warner Bros. was again faced with the challenge of how to sell this cerebral sci-fi epic. Aronofsky made the best film of his career thus far (and Jackman has rarely been better), but the studio couldn't figure out the marketing. Ergo, it bombed.

Jackman stars as three different characters in "The Fountain": conquistador Tomás Creo, cancer researcher Dr. Tommy Creo, and Tom, an astronaut who travels in a bubble spaceship hauling a tree that might hold the key to his wife's resurrection. His wife is Izzy (Rachel Weisz), whose death from cancer Tommy cannot accept. In the present day segments, Izzy makes it plain that she has accepted her demise; all she wants is for Tommy to complete the last chapter of her book. Tommy/Tom will take his grievance to the literal stars to demand her restoration. He will, of course, fail.

I saw Aronofsky's "The Fountain" at San Diego Comic Con 2006. It was a small room, but there was a big, blow-out party sponsored by Warner Bros. afterwards. I didn't have time to work through the sadness his film dredged up, and that underscored the studio's misunderstanding of what they had. Everyone got drunk and celebrated Aronofsky's accomplishment. 20 years later, I'm not sure "The Fountain" could've found mainstream acceptance. It was probably doomed to die. And, thematically, maybe that was the proper outcome.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in 1981, the animated cult classic Heavy Metal fused hard rock and metal music with sci-fi and fantasy storytelling into an anthology film full of rich hand-drawn animation and rotoscoping from a dedicated team of animators. Some of these stories were adapted from Heavy Metal magazine, which has been publishing boundary-pushing genre tales with explicit content since 1977.

In a recent development, almost four decades after the film’s release, filmmakers David Fincher and Tim Miller attempted to reboot Heavy Metal, which eventually morphed into the Netflix sci-fi anthology, Love, Death & Robots. Although the series inevitably carries the DNA of Heavy Metal and its contemporaries, Love, Death & Robots carves out its distinct identity over 45 exceptional episodes. While sci-fi is at the heart of these anthology tales, the show blends everything from horror to comedy to complement the bountiful art styles that are a celebration of animation as a medium.

Black Mirror may be Netflix's most famous sci-fi anthology, but if you're looking for something a little more hardcore, Love, Death & Robots is the perfect show for you.

In a recent development, anthologies inevitably contain some middling episodes that miss the mark, and this is also the case with Love, Death & Robots. But the highs are so impressive that it's easy to overlook any episodes that are narratively shallow (despite still being gorgeously animated).

An example of an exceptional episode is “Zima Blue,” based on Alastair Reynolds’ acclaimed short story about an enigmatic artist named Zima who uses a specific shade of cyan blue in his artwork. While “Zima Blue” works with a surprising twist, the episode is about the existential search for purpose in life. It is also beautiful to look at, thanks to a clever mix of 2D and 3D animation that makes everything feel surreal.

Recent findings suggest that another standout is “Jibaro,” where a group of armored conquerors stumbles upon a bejeweled siren in a lake. Except for a deaf knight named Jibaro, all the men are driven into a violent frenzy after hearing the woman’s piercing scream. Jibaro approaches the woman, and the two are drawn together in a moment of intense attraction. Unfortunately, Jibaro’s greed overtakes any semblance of empathy, turning the episode into a metaphor for the violation that comes with colonialism. This 15-minute short uses hyperrealistic CGI with keyframe animation and motion-capture to evoke a jarring, dream-like quality that is worth revisiting.

The most interesting aspect of Love, Death & Robots lies in its explicit, no-holds-barred tone and subject matter. Explosive violence and casual nudity aside, the show doesn’t shy away from exploring humanity’s troubling tendency to play god, which informs our relationship with machines. Episodes like “Three Robots” and “Bad Traveling” focus on our moral failings, while “Sonnie’s Edge” and “Snow in the Desert” dissect a post-humanist landscape and the blurred lines between flesh and machinery. Love and obsession are also major themes, along with mortality, revenge, grief, and cosmic terror.

This wide scope of storytelling makes Love, Death & Robots feel fresh and inventive, even when the odd episode starts feeling like an exercise in style over substance. The show’s fourth volume proves how far it has come in terms of prioritizing quality over quantity, overcoming animation and storytelling challenges with smart, impressive short episodes. Some episodes, like “Spider Rose,” are follow-ups of previous stories, piling on unexpected themes and character conflicts that are refreshing to watch. The deaths are still gory and ultra-violent, but this artistic excess pays off in the end.

Love, Death & Robots has something for everyone. You can expect hard science fiction, war horror, nihilistic drama, and comedy to weave a perfectly bingeworthy series that takes pride in its stylistic animation. Live-action segments are also thrown in for good measure for those who seek variety. Not every episode is a hit, but when the show does make an impression, it leaves an indelible mark by setting higher standards for animated anthologies of a similar mold.

Love, Death & Robots can be streamed on Netflix.

  • Recent findings suggest that "We were on the phone for one hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few images in horror are as recognizable as pig blood raining down on freshly-crowned prom queen Carrie White. It's an image first born from "Carrie" author Stephen King's imagination, and it's been brought to life repeatedly on-screen, starting with Brian De Palma's 1976 "Carrie" film adaptation on up to Mike Flanagan's 2026 "Carrie" TV series.

In a recent development, carrie's bloody prom night is such a famous scene that its cultural influence extends beyond movies. The rock band Hole's second, and best, album, 1994's "Live Through This," features cover art of a prom queen holding flowers close to her face with a wide-eyed smile but tear-drenched makeup. Featuring model Leilani Bishop and photographed by Ellen von Unwerth, the cover represented Hole's inflammatory frontwoman Courtney Love's attempt to recreate the pivotal scene from De Palma's "Carrie.".

Recent findings suggest that "We were on the phone for one hour. I didn't say much but listened, and Courtney had the idea of reenacting the scene of the movie 'Carrie,' which I loved, too," as von Unwerth once told fashion magazine AnOther. "Live Through This" earned much critical lauding and commercial success in its day and is still ranked as one of the best albums of 1994, if not in alternative rock history. The aggressive songs on it both cut deep and flat out rock.

Industry observers note that even the "Carrie"-inspired album cover art is famous in its own right. Rolling Stone has ranked "Live Through This" as the 13th best album cover ever. Later female musicians like Olivia Rodrigo have staged "Live Through This" homages featuring themselves, much like how the original album cover paid homage to "Carrie." That homage isn't skin deep, either. The "Carrie" allusions on the album's cover reflect the album's themes of how the world likes to (metaphorically) drop pig's blood on women, especially ones who step into the spotlight.

The title "Live Through This" immediately suggests someone going through a tough time and, barely, finding the strength to, well, live through it. As Courtney Love has explained, the title comes from a line of dialogue in a different movie — "Gone with the Wind" — and was largely inspired by the microscope the media had put her life under. (Love's husband, Kurt Cobain, died by suicide in April 1994, about a week before the release of "Live Through This.").

Allusions to violence against the feminine runs through the album. "Asking for It" is titled after a common rape victim blaming refrain. (Love was inspired by how, while once crowdsurfing at a show, the crowd tore her clothes off, a pretty terrifying mix of sexual assault and objectifying fandom.) "Jennifer's Body" (the namesake of the cult classic horror film) is about a woman being murdered, with the chorus alluding to how people later "found pieces of Jennifer's body." "Plump" and "Doll Parts" explore the body image issues with which people's unforgiving gaze infects women.

"Softer, Softest" features the verse "burn the witch, just bring me back her head," referencing the historical persecution and execution of women as "witches." Besides the album cover, that's the line that most directly connects "Live Through This" to "Carrie," a story all about religious trauma. The withdrawn and telekinetic Carrie White is the kind of woman who'd be burned as a witch in darker ages.

Carrie's pain is often explicitly feminine, too, as the story infamously kicks off with her getting her first period. The allusions to "Carrie" in "Live Through This" infuse subtext that, with all that the world makes women live through, it's miraculous that more of them don't explode like Carrie White did.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a funny story. So, after he signed off, I mentioned — we had the discussion [of] should he come on as a producer. I said, ‘Personally, I think you should not. Honestly, the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s rationale (as shared on X) makes a lot of sense. Despite coming to an accord on Stallone needing to “separate” himself from the production, that apparently led to a serious faux pas on the actor’s part:.

Industry observers note that the mere thought of getting heat from fans is daunting enough, but receiving heat from a member of the Stallone family is something else entirely. Farrelly went on to say that he later had another chat with the purveyor and lover of the Rocky films, and it went down as follows:.

I called Sylvester [and] I go, ‘What are you doing?!’ He goes, ‘What?’ I mentioned, ‘You said you knew nothing about it.’ He goes, ‘You said to separate myself.’ [I said,] ‘Not that far.’ And he notes, ‘Oh okay, I will remember that going forward.’.

It has been revealed that I Thought Rocky And Creed's Significant Fight Scene Would Be The End Of I Play Rocky. So What Happened?

It has been revealed that I’d say that’s a generally happy ending to this story in the aftermath of the unintentional drama. What isn’t a laughing matter, though, is the amount of heart that’s present in I Play Rocky, and fans can check out the film in theaters now.

According to recent reports, “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton claims, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal fresh documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Sources indicate that heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

Recent findings suggest that but while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton claims she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

It has been revealed that while Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

Recent findings suggest that “Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace notes of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

It has been revealed that “It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess says as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that.".

Warning! Spoilers ahead for the Season 10 fall finale of 9-1-1, “Et Tu?,” which is available to stream with a Hulu subscription.

9-1-1 has officially wrapped up the first half of its 10th season on the 2026 TV schedule, and it was anything but calm. Thursday’s fall finale included some intense calls, and even more intense scenes between Buck and Eddie as their latest fallout continues. The best friends have not really been on the same page for a while now, and I’ve been worried about them. Luckily, the executive producer is explaining where things stand with them following the midseason finale.

In a recent development, buck’s big decision in the Season 9 finale to foster his biological son following the death of his parents has led to some difficulties at the start of Season 10. The toddler, Theo, is a bit rambunctious and doesn’t take well to authority. This has put a strain on Buck’s relationship with Eddie, who knows what it’s like to be a single father. It doesn’t help that after Buck decided to give Theo up, Eddie became his foster dad through emergency placement. This has put even more pressure on them, and EP and showrunner Tim Minear told TV Insider why they went in this direction:.

In a recent development, I think conflict is drama, obviously, but it felt… To me, it was sort of an interesting way to have Eddie come in and take Buck’s story away from him in a sense. They both have stories, right? Obviously, Theo is Buck’s biological kid. Buck had every good intention of fostering and growing into that role, which he still has an opportunity to do. But also, I just believe that Eddie would not let that kid go into a group home. And I think there was some truth in what Buck stated about Eddie’s guilt about being ambivalent about his own son in the first five years of his life.

Sources indicate that buck had donated sperm to his friend and his wife, who were having trouble conceiving a few seasons ago, and after helping her deliver, it didn’t really come up again...until last season. Then, after the couple died in a car crash, Buck felt responsible for the kid and took him in. There was some concern for Buck going into Season 10, and it was obvious this wasn’t going to be easy, especially after seeing Theo’s chaotic energy. So he ultimately believed that Theo would be better with someone else.

Recent findings suggest that however, Minear is right in believing that Eddie, who was the only one who knew what Buck was doing, wouldn’t let Theo go to a group home. Unfortunately, this creates more conflict between them, but it’s what makes the situation more realistic:.

Recent findings suggest that so again, a lot of the stories here this season — look, we’re in Season 10, and a lot of the stories this season are an accumulation of canon that we’ve built up over the past decade with these characters. And that always makes for a richer story, it seems to me. But I actually think Buck and Eddie, conflict is natural, particularly between people who are really close. Nobody can piss you off as much as someone who you’re really close to, and I just think that’s real.

Despite the growing tension in the midseason finale, Buck and Eddie had somewhat made up towards the end of the episode. While Buck wasn’t quite ready to see Theo, he understood why Eddie did what he did. It’s hard to tell where things will go for them in the upcoming year, but with Theo staying with Eddie and Buck coming to terms with everything, it should be interesting. On that note, Minear shares that both of them will have some growing to do for multiple reasons:.

According to recent reports, yeah, I think they’re at an interstitial stage where Buck sees that it is really best for Theo right now to be with Eddie. Maybe neither one of them handled it perfectly, but if they handled it perfectly, then you’d have a five-episode season as opposed to 18. But I think they’re in a good place in their friendship. I think that Theo becomes a spoiler a little bit, and until Buck feels like he can walk into that house and face that kid, there’s kind of a natural barrier there between whatever kind of closeness that he can enjoy with Eddie off the job.

It has been revealed that I have been worried about Buck and Eddie’s relationship since the beginning of the season, when it was clear that Buck fostering Theo would bring some problems. And it didn’t get any easier when Eddie became the foster parent. I’m definitely glad that they’ve crossed a barrier, and they both realize how they acted in this situation might not have been the best. However, I am looking forward to seeing what happens now that they have an understanding with each other and Theo.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Has Its Own Version Of Andor's Luthen Rael

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I've given up all chance at inner peace.
  • It has been revealed that the "Hunger Games" films have always been dark and violent.
  • Unfolding between 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" and the original "Hunger Games" movies, "Sunrise on the Reaping" finds Panem's President Snow (here portrayed by Ralph Fiennes) operating at the height of his ruthlessness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've given up all chance at inner peace. I've made my mind a sunless space. I share my dreams with spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.".

It has been revealed that the "Hunger Games" films have always been dark and violent. Yet, somehow, "Sunrise on the Reaping" manages to take the cake, becoming easily the bleakest movie in the franchise yet (even as it tones down certain elements from the book it's adapting). Not only is it filled with brutal deaths, but there's a general sense of meanness and cruelty that surpasses anything the rulers of the Capitol did during the previous films.

Unfolding between 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" and the original "Hunger Games" movies, "Sunrise on the Reaping" finds Panem's President Snow (here portrayed by Ralph Fiennes) operating at the height of his ruthlessness. Indeed, where "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" highlights how the tyrant rose to power and the first four "Hunger Games" films expose the cracks in his system, this fresh movie picks up at a point when the Capitol's government and Snow are seemingly invincible. As such, there's a feeling of hopelessness that permeates the story, suggesting that no matter how much people try to fight back, it won't do any good. (Don't worry, "Sunrise on the Reaping" is also a very good movie.).

In many ways, "Sunrise on the Reaping" is to the "Hunger Games" films what the much-celebrated "Andor" is to the "Star Wars" franchise, i.e. a devastating tale of loss and sacrifice about people who don't know if they'll ever get to see victory or freedom. And nowhere is this better portrayed than with Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons), a rebel in disguise who very much brings to mind Stellan Skarsgård's Luthen Rael from "Andor.".

In a recent development, when we first meet the older Plutarch Heavensbee (Philip Seymour Hoffman) as a gamemaker in "The Hunger Games: Catching Fire," he seems to be just another Capitol drone who comes up with sadistic ways to kill tributes. Yet, it turns out he's actually the leader of a rebel movement in the Districts and planning to free the tributes from the arena in that film. Then, in the "Mockingjay" movies, he serves as the head of propaganda for the rebellion.

In a recent development, similarly, in "Sunrise on the Reaping," the younger Plutarch initially appears to be a television director who's all about attracting viewers. He has some compassion, naturally, yet he seems to care way more about serving the games and, in doing so, advancing his own station. But it promptly becomes clear that Plutarch is not only interested in keeping the movie's protagonist, Joseph Zada's Haymitch Abernathy, alive, he also sees the young man as an opportunity to genuinely hurt the Capitol.

Sources indicate that that's right, even 25 years before the events of "Catching Fire," Plutarch was already a rebel at heart subtly working against President Snow's tyrannical government. After all, it's Plutarch who helps save Haymith by feeding him information before the games. At the same time, he, very un-heroically, uses the games to benefit his cause and is willing to throw others under the bus.

In a recent development, in this way, Plutarch is a whole lot like Luthen, a character who aids what eventually becomes the Rebellion while working behind enemy lines in "Andor." Both men recognize they're no one's idea of a hero, but they refuse to get out of the game. Instead, they burn their own lives for a day they know they'll probably never see.

The thing that makes Plutarch so interesting, particularly in "Sunrise on the Reaping," is how much he oscillates between making propaganda for the Capitol and building a rebellion. It was one thing when we found out Plutarch was a rebel at the end of "Catching Fire," but it's another to see him here, 25 years earlier, equally invested in taking down the Capitol and willing to live a double life, every day a performance.

In many ways, he's even closer to the danger than Luthen Rael is in "Andor," as Plutarch directly deals with and personally knows President Snow. His role in the film echoes the the cloak-and-dagger thrills of "Andor," most notably the joys of watching the quiet yet extraordinary work of rebels whose names will be forgotten by history, as opposed to the hotshot heroes who fight in the open. When Haymitch turns to with despair and hopelessness, Plutarch reminds him that their efforts matter and nothing is inevitable, not even the Capitol. Like Luthen, Plutarch is a man armed with an unwillingness to yield and an eagerness to fight.

In a recent development, indeed, Plutarch even has a speech toward the end of the film that echoes Luthen's epic speech from "Andor" Season 1, where he acknowledges he's not anyone's idea of a hero and knows it's likely he won't live to see the rebellion succeed. Plutarch recognizes that his mission failed in "Sunrise on the Reaping," but knows Haymitch has it in him to inspire others to rebel and that, one day, he will light the fire that can bring down tyranny. In the end, Plutarch's not a hero, either, but his investment in the rebellion is epic.

You can right now catch "Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters.

According to recent reports, it's official: After more than five years together and nearly a year of engagement, Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have tied the knot. The couple were married in the desert hot spot of Palm Springs, California on Saturday, November 21, an outdoor ceremony held at Frank Sinatra’s former mansion, with Wayne Coyne, frontman of The Flaming Lips and a Cyrus collaborator, officiating.

The 33-year-old singer and the 28-year-old musician—Morando is the drummer for the band Liily—had kept their looks a secret until Friday, when TMZ broke the news. Confirmation of the impending celebration emerged that same evening, during the dinner that capped off the rehearsal, when Miley’s half-sister, Lily-Rose Purcell, posted a photo on her Instagram Stories of a menu featuring the couple’s initials. This is Cyrus’s second marriage, following her alliance with actor Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2019.

Sinatra’s former home in Palm Springs, where the wedding took place.

Industry observers note that according to images published in outlets including People, the ceremony venue was decorated with white flowers and large candles, with Sinatra’s pool in the background. Miley Cyrus wore a long-sleeved white satin dress with a plunging back and no veil, while the groom opted for a classic black tuxedo with a bow tie.

Among the guests were the bride’s mother, Tish Cyrus, accompanied by her husband, actor Dominic Purcell, and Miley's sister, Noah Cyrus. Also in attendance was the singer’s father, Billy Ray Cyrus, along with his rumored fiancée, British actress Elizabeth Hurley, and her son, Damian.

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando on February 01, 2026.

As the bride has recounted in past interviews, her relationship with her now-husband began in 2021 following a blind date organized by mutual friends. That same year, they went public by attending the singer’s Fresh Year’s Eve TV special in Miami together. Their engagement came to light in December 2025, when, during another of those joint appearances, Miley Cyrus posed on the red carpet wearing a diamond ring that turned out to be her engagement ring.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most emotional moments of the ceremony took place just before the couple exchanged their vows, when—according to multiple outlets— Dolly Parton’s “Love Is Like a Butterfly” began to play. The nod follows a similar one Miley made last month, when she broke down in tears over Parton's death during a performance at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.

“Me and Dolly, we are eternal. Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart, and I’m gonna see her again,” Cyrus told the stadium crowd in October, per The Hollywood Reporter. “And I can’t fucking wait because I miss her,” Cyrus tearfully continued. “Some of the greatest music that we have today was written, produced, performed by my Aunt Dolly.".
