📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something new. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

It has been revealed that that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

It has been revealed that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

To make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

With a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but says you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

Industry observers note that here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

The finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a upcoming window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

Industry observers note that I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

According to recent reports, everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

For something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

It has been revealed that I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

Maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a significant family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a fresh website.

Industry observers note that bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

Sources indicate that it looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

Todd Boehly gave an insight into his no nonsense approach to investing in sports and entertainment in the concluding fireside chat of the Qatar Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days over the weekend.

The billionaire investor’s holding company Eldridge has some $75B in assets including stakes in Backrooms distributor A24, and Fulwell Entertainment as well as the Los Angeles Lakers, the Los Angeles Sparks, the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Trent Rockets among many more.

The holding is also a partner with Deadline owner Penske Media in the Penske Media Eldridge unit encompassing live TV entertainment specialist Dick Clark Productions as well as events such as the Golden Globes and SXSW. Related Stories News Joe Russo Talks 'Doomsday' Teaser-Trailer Strategy Ahead Of Rumored Monday Drop: "I Have To interact With Fans" News Watermelon Expands Production Ambitions As It Seals Partnership With Qatar's Film Committee.

In a recent development, boehly first connected with A24 cofounder Daniel Katz, when the latter headed Guggenheim Partners’ film finance group in Latest York, while he was president of the global investment firm before leaving to create Eldridge. Watch on Deadline.

“One of the things I believe is that there’s very few entertainment people that understand math… the math of entertainment is really about understanding how are you taking risk and then how are you distributing risk,” he noted in the chat entitled “Playing to Win”.

“It’s no different than any other industry, if you’re thinking about what amount of risk you are willing to take and then how are you going to feed that risk,” he added.

Boehly stated Katz had impressed him from the start for his ability to identify and work with risk during his time with Guggenheim Partners.

“Daniel’s real magic, when he worked on our trading floor from, let’s call it like 2008 to 2012, he didn’t take a lot of risks, but he said ‘no’ a lot,” he said.

In a recent development, “There was a slate that was done by a group called Stark Investments, and one of their significant films was Poseidon. I remember it indicated up on our desk. And Daniel was immediately like, this is a disaster. It’s going to cost so much money, you know, they’re not going to be able to make any return on it.”.

The $160M disaster movie by Wolfgang Petersen went down in film financing folklore after it faltered at the box office and failed to gross enough to cover its P&A costs.

Industry observers note that boehly provided $19M in seed money for A24 as Katz launched the company in 2012 with David Fenkel and Joh Hodges. It was last publicly valued at $3.5 billion in June 2024.

“Everyone told me in Hollywood that there’s no room for another distribution company,” recalled the businessman. “His early successes with Spring Breakers and The Bling Ring were really structured finance trades.”.

“You’re not really allowed to talk about that in the entertainment world because everything’s creative and creator driven… what Daniel was really good at, because he sat on a trading desk and he understood risk and he understood math, he was really good at figuring out how am I going to get my money back using different windows.”.

Starring James Franco, Selena Gomez, Vanessa Hudgens, Harmony Korine’s Spring Breakers premiered in competition in Venice and went on to gross $31M.

“Spring Breakers cost a couple million bucks to buy, and he ended up making 10 million bucks or so very swiftly on, because he really understood that it’s a structured finance straight,” mentioned Boehly.

He added that beyond Katz’s business savviness, the company had also understood how to tap into social media to generate audience engagement as well as how to plug into trends of the moment.

Industry observers note that “One of the things that A24 has done an amazing job at is being able to read the cultural zeitgeist. I think Civil War was really well timed; Marty Supreme was very well timed with Timothée Chalamet and his ascension as probably one of the top actors for the next couple of decades.”.

Boehly also highlighted A24’s strategy of growing a cohort of directors and actors, who returned to work with the organization on a regular basis.

“He wants repeat customers. He wants the directors coming back… he wants the actors coming back… because then it’s not a transaction, it becomes a recurring business with enterprise,” mentioned Boehly.

In a recent development, “So many people think about the film business, ‘Oh, it’s a transaction’. But if you’re really thinking about how to build an enterprise, then you need to make sure that you have a recurring revenue base. And the way you do that in this industry is you get repeat owners.”.

He also gave insight into how Katz constructs A24’s slate in a way that enables it to work with established names and newcomers and turn a profit, suggesting that over a portfolio of 15 films, nine would be “the core bread and butter”.

“It’s a budget of 25 to 40 million bucks. It’s the expectation that he’s going to make 1.35 times,” he explained. “And if you think about the math of it again, you get 0.8 times your money back right away or very promptly. So, when you think about the risk that you have, you’re in for 0.2. If you make 1.35 and your risk capital is 0.2, but you’re going to make six, seven times that 0.2.”.

“And then he’ll take three significant swings and make something that has the capacity to become multiple films out of the content… he’ll take 1.2 times. So, he’ll modify his expectations on the rate of return to achieve something that might have more enterprise value or longevity on the back of it.”.

Boehly suggested the final three films would be by up-and-coming young directors, and would require time, energy and effort rather than big financial investments and risk.

“He’s always thinking about how do I build that portfolio in order to have my bread and butter, have the opportunity to have something that’s got longevity and then find someone who’s going to be special in the industry,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that netflix's newest streaming hit, The Body, is drawing in millions of viewers, great reviews, and a gaggle of protests from people who didn't much care for the trailer. But if your lesbian-forward supernatural horror series isn't drawing cries of "blasphemy!"...what are you even doing? In that spirit, we'll conjure up some other demonstrates dealing with the (extremely) dark side of high school.

According to recent reports, this time-hopping survival drama is about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive—the extent of which we only learn about via flashbacks from the present day, where the events of 19 months spent in the wild continue to resonate. There are ambiguous teases of the supernatural here (much more ambiguous than in The Body), but there's plenty of human-level horror as well. The show explores the nasty things we get up to when in survival mode (whether trapped in the wilds, stuck with other teenagers—or god forbid both at once), while also cynically (but accurately) positing that there's a huge difference between the version of the past we talk about and the one that really happened. Stream Yellowjackets on Paramount+.

According to recent reports, situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It swiftly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, and the ways in which we'll do just about anything when survival is on the line. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, when pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

Juicy import Elite follows a group of working-class friends who earn scholarships to Las Encinas, a fictional private school that is, in the show’s universe, the most exclusive in Spain. What they find there is snobbery, mystery, murder, and lots and lots of sex (between and among characters of various sexual orientations and numerical groupings). The smart, wonderfully trashy show ran for a shocking (in our modern streaming era) eight seasons, with a couple of regional remakes. There's no supernatural stuff here, but plenty of dark deeds done with youthful vigor. Stream Elite on Netflix.

A teenager, Mae (Madeleine Arthur), is discovered by the side of the road with weird religious symbols carved into her skin. The hospital psychiatrist who treats her (Emily Deschanel) takes pity on, and interest in, Mae, deciding to take her in while arrangements can be made for a more permanent home for the cult escapee. Mae is, after all, level-headed and quiet, and couldn't possibly be any trouble. Hoo boy, yeah, that turns out to be a bad call on the good doctor's part. Stream Devil in Ohio on Netflix.

Industry observers note that A different type of blasphemy at play here, in that Joan Lindsay's novel was already adapted brilliantly by Peter Weir in 1975, in a film often referred to as the greatest to come out of Australia. And yet, this Natalie Dormer-lead take is an achievement in its own right, the extended running time of a miniseries offering up more time to sit with the story's deliberately ineffable mysteries. Dormer plays Hester Appleyard, headmistress of a school for young ladies in the Australian bush. It's going well until a Valentine's Day picnic to the title's Hanging Rock sees three students and a governess disappear, impossibly, without a trace, bringing about the slow unravelling of pretty much everyone left behind. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on Prime Video and Tubi.

According to recent reports, mariam (Andria Tayeh) is brutally bullied by the cool clique at her private school in this Jordanian import, a high school drama that's both universal and distinctly Muslim in character. Fed up, Mariam convinces a couple of similarly outcast friends to join forces with her in a revenge plot that quickly gets out of hand. The show deals with Jordanian-style patriarchy head-on, without drawing any easy conclusions about its characters—Mariam catfishes one of her bullies and convinces her to send a revealing picture, one that she immediately posts, exploiting the very same repressive cultural elements that she claims to deplore. It's a smart, realist drama with soapy elements and nothing by way of the supernatural, but it's still a very sharp picture of the extremely cutthroat nature of high school life. Stream AlRawabi School for Girls on Netflix.

Peyton List stars as Maddie, a teenager in small-town Wisconsin for whom her death is very much just the beginning. Stuck in a high school in the afterlife (because hell is definitely for children), she goes on a journey to solve her own murder while uncovering secrets and lies in both worlds. It all sounds a bit grim, but the show has a sense of fun about it: While Maddie does develop the ability to communicate with the living, her world is populated by ghost teens from various eras and generations, with customs, mores, and cliques having developed in ghost high school just as in our world. Stream School Spirits on Paramount+.

Industry observers note that the new Girigo app, claiming to grant wishes, sounds like harmless fun. Except, of course, that the things that teenagers want aren't always beneficent, and the app has already been the conduit for some incredibly dark deeds by the time it gets into the hands of the five high schoolers who find themselves caught in a Ring-like web of shamanistic horror and death countdowns. This is why we tell you to put your phones down once in a while... Stream If Wishes Could Kill on Netflix.

Four one-time best friends reunite at Rosewood High School a year after the disappearance of the leader of their little clique, all having received threatening messages from the mysterious "A," who knows everything they did last summer...and pretty much all the rest of the time. Shoplifting, parents having affairs, students hooking up with teachers—you name it, it's happening in town, and A knows it all. After the prime suspect turns up dead, the girls are caught in the killer's web while trying to keep their secrets hidden. If seven juicy seasons and three A's aren't enough for you, there are three spin-offs. Stream Pretty Little Liars on Hulu and HBO Max.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade. It was Tommy in a white belt and eyeliner, vastly expanding the band’s sonic palette beyond the punk-thrash of their first two albums. It felt like the beginning of what should have been a long, ambitious upcoming phase of My Chem’s career, but instead, they released the underrated Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys in 2010 and broke up three years later.

Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by new music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.

Welcome to the Black Parade recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and a newly introduced vinyl edition made a surprise Number One debut. That album’s producer, Rob Cavallo (who also worked on much of Green Day‘s discography, among many other projects) joined Rolling Stone by Zoom for an in-depth look at the making of a 21st-century rock masterpiece.

What did My Chem first play for you that got you excited to be involved in this album?They were interviewing other guys as well, but I’ll never forget, ’cause it was so freezing cold in Upcoming York, and we went to SIR, and they played me a few things. But the one that blew my mind was “Mama.” When I heard that, I remember just jumping off the couch just going, “Oh, my God, you guys. That is so great and original,” and you could tell it was part of a deeper picture of something, even though I was new to the band. It felt key to me right away that this band was existing on a higher conceptual level.

Industry observers note that that song sounds like the Doors version of “Alabama Song.” It’s very un-punk at first, and then it kicks into the—The heavy part, right. Yeah, I kinda likened it in a weird way rhythmically to the Doors. I was also thinking of [the Rolling Stones’] “Mother’s Little Helper.” Almost like you could see the Cossacks-style Russian dancing to it. It’s like this sort of head-bopping thing that just felt very edgy, and very anti-establishment rock in a weird way. It was definitely like the we-don’t-give-a-fuck kind of rock. In a recent development, but then there was this story in there. I was like, “What is this guy going on about? What is happening here? This is heavy stuff.” So that’s why I jumped up off the couch on that song.

It has been revealed that and of course, a lot of the record at that point had not been written. And then I got this call and they stated, “Meet us at this steakhouse near SIR.” And I remember walking there and I thought my legs were gonna freeze off. And then we got in and we had the greatest dinner ever, and they said, “All right, you wanna be our producer?” I said, “Yeah, I do.” And that was it. They decided a couple hours after the first meeting.

Industry observers note that do you think your enthusiasm put it over the top for them? Obviously it couldn’t have hurt that you had just done American Idiot, which had similar levels of ambition.I think I was told that they liked what I said about the music, and they probably liked that I had done two records that I think stood out in their minds. Yeah, I had just done American Idiot, which was of course really major and was working, and I think they liked that. And then I think the other record they mentioned was Jawbreaker, Dear You, which is a band and an album that had an infamous history of being a dismal failure, in a way, commercially when it first came out.

Recent findings suggest that but also then received its just deserts many years later, in the fact that it was now considered one of the seminal emo records of all time. And of course, we all know the history about how the band got back together and then all of a sudden on one show there were 60,000 people singing every word to every song on that record. But at the same time we also know that Kurt Cobain was, like, one of their biggest supporters — they were opening for Nirvana. So it was kinda cool. To this day, I still remember that hallway going down to where the bedrooms were on the top floor, and it just looked like you were in the scariest movie. And the coat of arms and the polar bear, the stuffed polar bear, all the weird stuff that was just everywhere.

It was such an old building that we had to bring in space heaters, and so a lot of the writing actually ended up taking place over a couple of months in that particular space. And Mikey [Way] eventually, as you probably heard, he had to move out. He couldn’t take it after a while. It was just too scary.

In a recent development, but we had a lot of fun there, and we got a lot of the work done. So the record, I would say, was probably 90 percent written by the time, or 95 percent written by the time we got out of there and headed to the studio. With, of course, the notable exception of the song “Black Parade” itself, that has its own sort of strange and storied history.

Sources indicate that while they’re writing in the house, where are you and what are you doing?Every day, Monday through Friday, I’d show up with my engineer, Doug McKean, and I set up some fancy microphones in this giant, crazy living room that they had. The great room in that house looked like it was, like, 1,500 square feet. And we put the band in there with a PA, like a smaller PA, so that we could record whatever the band was writing and doing. So the writing was done almost live.

According to recent reports, gerard liked to just sing over the band. And someone would bring in a riff and we would just start jamming and recording. And the great news is that all of those recordings actually are now available online. I think there was a substantial box set of these live two-track recordings that are sort of the precursor — they’re the demos that we made the album from.

After surviving the Upside Down, Noah Schnapp apparently volunteered as tribute for the latest Hunger Games film.

Marking the opening weekend of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, the Stranger Things alum revealed that he auditioned to play Haymitch with a selfie in a blonde wig, admitting that Joseph Zada was the right choice.

“POV: my audition for Haymitch,” wrote Schnapp on his Instagram Story with some laughing emojis. “@josephzada think they picked right for this one.”.

Now playing in theaters, the Hunger Games prequel from director Francis Lawrence and writers Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie is based on Suzanne Collins’ 2025 novel Sunrise on the Reaping, set during Haymitch’s game in the Second Quarter Quell.

Starring Zada as Haymitch, Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before 2012’s The Hunger Games, in which Woody Harrelson originated the role. It follows 2023’s The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes in continuity, set 40 years later. Watch on Deadline.

The movie also stars Elle Fanning, McKenna Grace, Ben Wang, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Billy Porter, Maya Hawke, Kieran Culkin, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Lili Taylor and Ralph Fiennes.

Miley Cyrus and her fiancé Maxx Morando married Saturday at a wedding ceremony in Palm Springs, California.

Photos of the wedding emerged Saturday night, showing the pair exchanging nuptials while standing under an arch covered in white flowers. The Flaming Lips’ Wayne Coyne, Cyrus’ Dead Petz collaborator, reportedly officiated the ceremony.

Cyrus and Morando shared photos from the wedding on social media Sunday, making the knot-tying official:.

On Friday, members of the Cyrus clan — including mom Tish and sister Noah — were spotted gathering for the couple’s rehearsal dinner in Southern California; the daughter of Tish Cyrus’ husband revealed the rehearsal dinner on social media, TMZ reported. Billy Ray Cyrus was also in attendance for his daughter’s wedding, People reported.

Cyrus has since worked with Morando on songs from her last two albums, Endless Summer Vacation and Something Beautiful. If You Loved 'Yellowjackets,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that yellowjackets is a vibe.
  • Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.
  • The survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that yellowjackets is a vibe. The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying. The dual timelines build tension around the story’s many mysteries, and the complex characters (no one’s completely good or evil on this show) make for a lot of surprising plot swerves that feel grounded despite the supernatural implications all around them. If you’re looking for more of that specific flavor of horror, you should probably watch Alive.

Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.

The survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances. They use the wrecked plane as shelter in the withering cold, they scavenge for anything that could be useful, and they ration out the only food they have: Some chocolates and a case of wine. But an early mistake leaves them without any food at all, and slowly they come to the sickening realization that their best chance at survival is to treat the corpses of their friends and families scattered around the crash site as a food source.

Sources indicate that there’s no supernatural aspect, but the story has a similar tone of desperation and despair as Yellowjackets. These are people determined to survive in an impossible situation, and they do things that no one outside of their shared experience could possibly understand. The real-life origins of the story add a sense of horror that more than matches the fictional “It” that haunts the girls of Yellowjackets; putting yourself into that very real experience makes it clear just how terrified everyone was. Rent Alive on Prime Video.

If you’re craving more cannibals, cults, and crazies at the mercy of nature itself, here are a few more movies you should check out.

Industry observers note that if you want to watch a movie that is essentially an adaptation of Yellowjackets, check out Eden. Even though it was released years before the show, the stories are so similar (albeit largely gender-flipped) that the producers of Eden actually sued, claiming plagiarism (they lost). In the film, a men’s soccer team (and two women on the same plane) crash-land on a deserted island, and as they fight for survival, things descend into, yes, madness and cannibalism as the survivors suffer dwindling food and water supplies and the rise of two violently opposed factions. It’s not nearly as deeply imagined as Yellowjackets, and it doesn’t have the supernatural hints of the show, but if you want a truly similar story, it’s a good choice. Stream Eden on The Roku Channel, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

You obviously cannot discuss Yellowjackets without discussing Lord of the Flies, William Golding’s 1954 novel about a group of schoolboys who descend into brutality and savagery when they’re stranded on a deserted island. The book has been adapted many times, but the 1963 version directed by Peter Brook is still the best version. Brook managed to elicit remarkably naturalistic performances from his young actors, giving the story a realistic tone that is somehow more terrifying than any amount of horror vibes. Stream Lord of the Flies on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that A slower and more haunting story, Picnic at Hanging Rock explores some of the same themes as Yellowjackets in an entirely different way. On Valentine’s Day in the year 1900, several students and teachers from an all-girls private school in Victoria, Australia, head to Hanging Rock for a picnic. Four students head off to explore and fall inexplicably asleep, and then three vanish, along with one of the teachers. Dreamy and drenched in dread, the story never offers any easy answers, and it explores themes of invading natural areas where you’re not wanted, burgeoning (and confusing) adolescent sexuality, and how our fear of the unknowable warps our perspective and often diminishes our humanity. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

You can never really go wrong with a Hitchcock film, and if you’re looking for another story about a disparate group of people forced to make terrifying decisions in order to survive, watch Lifeboat (based on a story by John Steinbeck). One of the director’s most underrated films, it’s the story of a group of survivors in a lifeboat after a German U-boat sinks their ship during World War II (including one survivor from the German boat). It’s a masterful suspense engine that’s not afraid to have its characters discuss the moral and ethical quandaries facing them as they struggle to survive and maintain their humanity under a constant threat of death. Stream Lifeboat on Hoopla or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that if you love the supernatural aspects of Yellowjackets as the girls come to believe a force they call “It” is out in the woods, check out The Ritual. Four friends embark on a hike in the wilds of northern Sweden to honor their deceased friend. When one of them is injured, they leave the marked trail to take a shortcut through the forest—where they are soon forced to shelter in an abandoned cabin, just like the Yellowjackets—and things begin to slide into the terrifying when they encounter a cult worshipping an ancient deity that grants them immortality in exchange for human sacrifices. It’s as if the show was condensed to an hour-and-a-half and the terror quotient was turned way, way up. Stream The Ritual on Netflix.

50 Years Ago Today: The Beach Boys Play Pivotal ‘Brian’s Back’ Concert in Cincinnati

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that “Brian is the Beach Boys, and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band.
  • It has been revealed that just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence.
  • The Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their newly introduced work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that “Brian is the Beach Boys, and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band. “We’re thrilled to have him back.”.

It has been revealed that just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence. But the Beach Boys were the beneficiaries of an enormous nostalgia wave that swept America in the mid-1970s, giving us American Graffiti, Happy Days, Sha Na Na, and Grease.

The Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their newly introduced work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974. As a result, they dumped most of the recent material from their live repertoire and began playing arenas and even stadiums. “We knocked them dead every time we went out just playing the hits,” Al Jardine told Rolling Stone in 2025. “It allowed us to grow musically at home while we could continue to entertain. It was a nice balance.”.

But by 1976, as Endless Summer mania began petering out, the group needed a newly introduced gambit to keep drawing the major crowds. That’s why band manager Steve Love decided to rouse Brian Wilson from his bed and get him back on the road for the first time since 1964, generating a groundswell of interest in the band.

Recent findings suggest that they promoted the “Brian’s Back” campaign with an NBC television special put together by Lorne Michaels and the original Saturday Night Live team, which included a legendary sketch where Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi storm into Brian’s bedroom as the “Surf Police” and force him to surf for the first time. Annie Leibovitz shot a classic photo of Wilson standing on the sand that day in his blue robe, which appeared on the Nov. 4, 1976, cover of Rolling Stone.

Much of the press outside of Rolling Stone presented Wilson as a goofy eccentric rather than a genuine genius. “Brian is like an amiable child (violence was never one of his symptoms) trying to relearn the simple social graces,” People wrote. “As Brian told Mike [Love] lately, ‘I’m tired of being a failure.'” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

According to recent reports, that’s why he decided not only to join the tour but also to produce a new Beach Boys record for the first time since Pet Sounds. The result was the underwhelming 15 Major Ones, which is thin on new originals and heavy on classic covers like Chuck Berry’s “Rock and Roll Music,” the Dixie Cups’ “Chapel of Love,” and Fats Domino’s “Blueberry Hill.”.

In a recent development, brian Wilson was an infrequent presence throughout their demonstrates in the summer of 1976, but fully committed to a winter tour in November and December that followed a two-month hiatus from the road, giving him time to record The Beach Boys Love You. The run of dates began Nov. 22 at the Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati, Ohio. Tickets ($7.50 in advance and $8.50 on show day) were unreserved throughout the entire venue, which encouraged fans to line up all day to secure choice spots.

Industry observers note that (Three years later, 11 Who fans were trampled to death when doors opened at this same venue. As a result, Cincinnati outlawed “festival seating” at concerts. The ban wouldn’t be lifted until 2002, when Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band played an arena show at the U.S. Bank Arena on the Rising tour.).

The Beach Boys show opens with “Wouldn’t It Be Nice” and “Palisades Park,” before Mike Love welcomes “my cousin, the one and only, the magnificent, Brian Wilson!” The crowd roars as he briefly stands up from his perch behind the piano, and then they kick into “Little Deuce Coupe,” “Darlin’,” “In My Room,” and “God Only Knows” while the crowd squeals with delight. Related Content Al Jardine Writes Open Letter to Fellow Beach Boy Mike Love: 'Praying For Your Recovery' Watch John Stamos and the California Sound Substitute for an Ailing Mike Love at Epcot Center The Beach Boys Cancel Final 2026 Concert The Beach Boys Canceled Another Show. A John Stamos Spinoff Group Is Taking Their Spot.

“Brian was introduced early on in the first set, and most of the crowd stood to acknowledge one of the giants in the history of rock,” noted a review by Dennis Freeman of the News Record. “He didn’t do much, sat impassively behind his piano, but it was key to the group that he was with them again.”.

It has been revealed that after warming the crowd up with oldies, they shifted the show to the present with Al Jardine’s “Back Home” from 15 Substantial Ones. It goes over particularly well with this crowd since it’s all about going back to Jardine’s birthplace of Ohio. “Well, I’m going back this summer to Ohio,” he sings. “I’m going to seek out all my friends I’ve always known/I’m going back to that farm that I remember.” (The song fell out of the band’s rotation in 1978 and wasn’t brought back until a Jardine and the Pet Sounds Band concert in Warren, Ohio, earlier this year.).

“How would you like to hear a couple of new ones we haven’t even done for the public yet?” Mike Love asks the crowd after “Back Home.” “These aren’t even released yet. They will be out in January on our new album. Keep it quiet and don’t go singing to too many groups since they might rip it off. The first one we’re going to do is called ‘Love Is a Woman.’ It sends chills up and down where I won’t tell you. The other one is a song about being on an airplane, so we call it ‘Airplane.’ So listen real good. We hope you like it.”.

Sources indicate that nobody in the arena had any idea they were witnessing a historic moment. This was the first time anyone outside the tight Beach Boys circle had heard even a note of music from The Beach Boys Love You. And even though many fans likely used this as an opportunity to run to the bathroom or grab a beer, the group did a magnificent job on both. “Airplane” is especially transcendent. (Sadly, they’d only play Love You songs a handful more times, and they wouldn’t go near any of it after 1979. It wasn’t until Al Jardine’s inaugural tour with the Pet Sounds Band in 2025 that Love You finally got the treatment it deserved in front of live audiences.).

They win the audience back with a trio of 1960s songs (“Catch a Wave,” “Heroes and Villains,” and “Surfin’ USA”) before introducing the crowd to a local woman named Joellyn Lambert, a former taxi driver who drove Jardine through town in 1970 and inspired his song “Susie Cincinnati.” They recorded it for 15 Significant Ones and placed an ad in the local paper prior to the show seeking her out. “Attention!!!” reads the notice. “The Beach Boys are looking for the lady cab driver named Suzi who picked them up six years from the airport. Group wants the person to be guest at their November 22 concert at Riverfront Coliseum.”.

Lambert was stunned when the Cincinnati Post tracked her down and arranged the visit. “I still can’t believe this is really happening,” she told the paper. “I’m now stopped on the street and asked if I’m really ‘Susie Cincinnati.'”.

The deep cuts continued with “It’s Okay,” “A Casual Look,” “Feel Flows,” and “Everyone’s in Love With You” before they closed out the night with a long run of surf-era hits that finished with “Fun, Fun, Fun.”.

“We danced, clapped and sang our way through classic after classic, each song bringing back memories of summers past,” wrote Freeman in the News Record. “‘Surfer Girl’ led into ‘California Girls’ and climaxed with ‘Good Vibrations.’ The audience was pretty young, mainly 18-year-olds, and it was fascinating to note the songs which were greeted with the most applause were the group’s early pre-Beatles hits.”.

“It shows the timelessness of the Beach Boys’ music,” he continued. “It also indicates that rock critics are wrong that time is up for the group. Even if the apparent re-emergence of the group as a creative force is short-lived, be assured the people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.”.

They would indeed. But what they didn’t want to hear or see was basically any song they recorded after “Do It Again.” Those fans were in luck since the Beach Boys essentially abandoned any pretense that they were anything but a perpetual-motion 1960s jukebox not long after the 1976 Brian’s Back tour. The idea of seven songs from a fresh album and another two from an album that wasn’t even released yet, as they did in Cincinnati, soon became unthinkable. Trending Stories Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Marry at Palm Springs Wedding Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special Boy George on His Israel Trip: 'I Wasn't Able to Not Say Something'.

It has been revealed that the Beach Boys returned to Cincinnati on Oct. 10 of this year for a show at the PNC Pavilion at Riverbend. Love is now the final legit member in the touring lineup, and this was a deeply upsetting concert for many fans since it was the first one where he was unable to stand or even sing. He’s been battling a severe health ailment for at least the past year and hasn’t been seen since a show the following night in Nashville.

According to recent reports, whatever happens going forward, the News Record was prophetic back in 1976 when it said “people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.” Does that mean they’ll become a zombie group like Foreigner or the Four Tops that continues to tour without any original members? Could Jardine finally be given the chance to front his own version of the Beach Boys? Are their children going to take over? There’s simply no way to know at this point. But it’s very hard to imagine a summer passing without some version of the Beach Boys on the road.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

It has been revealed that if you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an problem with the Duo itself.

Industry observers note that I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

In a recent development, I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for highlights and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that after a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

Sources indicate that I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

It has been revealed that I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Recent findings suggest that is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

Sources indicate that the iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique new iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

What has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Those two characters carrying that cake on Broadway will continue toting after the production closes: Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across Fresh York) will move to the Off Broadway venue New World Stages this spring.

The current Broadway cast of Sam Tutty and Christiani Pitts is not expected to make the move; new casting for the Off Broadway staging has not been revealed.

Nominated for eight Tony Awards, the musical, written and composed by Jim Barne and Kit Buchan, will begin previews Monday, March 22, 2027, at Fresh World – just a couple blocks from the Longacre Theatre, its current Broadway home – with an opening night of Sunday, April 4, 2027.

The Broadway staging is set to play its final performance on Sunday, November 29. Watch on Deadline.

The move was announced at the curtain call following today’s Broadway performance.

Directed & choreographed by Tim Jackson, Two Strangers opened on Broadway on November 20, 2025, starring Tutty and Pitts as, respectively, a starry-eyed, optimistic young British man and a sharp, no-nonsense Newly introduced Yorker who are thrown together when they prepare to attend a wedding, for which they must complete the task that gives the romantic comedy its title.

The Off Broadway production of Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across Fresh York) will feature scenic and costume design by Soutra Gilmour; lighting design by Jack Knowles; sound design by Tony Gayle; orchestrations by Lux Pyramid; and music supervision by Nick Finlow.

The musical is produced Off Broadway by Kevin McCollum, Tim Johanson, Glass Half Full Productions, and Jamie Wilson Productions.

Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Industry observers note that then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Industry observers note that alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

Industry observers note that apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that “I’ve always joked that I’m a little bit Jew-ish-ish with a significant hyphen,” notes Culture Club frontman Boy George. He had recently returned from an eight-day trip to Israel, where he performed two sold-out shows at Tel Aviv’s Menora Mivtachim Arena on Nov. 4 and 7. George’s arrival is a rare one, as most Western artists have steered clear of the country, which has been plagued by political infighting, wars in Gaza and Iran, and global criticism for its handling of the conflicts.

Sources indicate that but the 65-year-old is defying convention with characteristic flair. George burst on the pop scene in 1982, one of the first MTV stars with the Upcoming Wave hit “Do You Really Want to Hurt Me?” Challenging gender and cultural norms in an oversize hat, Rasta dreads, drag makeup, and a T-shirt that spelled Culture Club in Hebrew (Havurat Aguda), Boy George was an instant sensation and ruled the pop charts for years to come.

In a recent development, four decades later, Boy George is still advocating for multiculturalism and LGBTQ+ rights, but his hometown of London feels less tolerant. On his way to the doctor in April, he arrived at the Jewish neighborhood of Golder’s Green moments in the wake of an antisemitic stabbing spree, the culmination of a disturbing 82 percent uptick in physical assaults in the U.K. in the first half of 2026, per the Community Security Trust. He then visited the Nova exhibit in London and released the reggae-infused single “We Will Dance Again” (Od Nirkod in Hebrew) in late July on Instagram and X. He made his position clear through the lyrics: “You say genocide/I say war…. You condemn the Jews with selective memory/Musicians holding flags, mouthing like sheep…. You never mention Oct. 7/Young girls raped against trees, murdered brutally/For the crime of dancing.”.

In a recent development, the song prompted a swift and harsh backlash. He remarked he “parted ways” with longtime manager of his BGP label, Tony Pontius, was removed from Bandcamp for using AI on the track, lost old friends like Human League and Heaven 17 founder Martyn Ware, was disinvited from a memorial honoring stylist friend Pam Hogg, and was pulled from a West End revival of “Jesus Christ Superstar.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Sources indicate that never one to back down, George spoke out, released his single with live instrumentation on Warner Music/ADA in October (it charted in the U.K., France, Greece, and Latvia), and announced he would perform in Israel, boycotts be damned. While there, he met with Oct. 7 survivors, victims’ families and held a press conference at the site of the Nova Festival in Re’im, where Hamas killed 378 concertgoers and staff, took 44 hostages, and sexually assaulted concertgoers, according to an independent U.N. investigation.

Upon his return to London, George reflected on his trip, the blowback he received, and the alarming rise in antisemitism in an interview with Rolling Stone.

Is it true that “We Will Dance Again” was inspired by your visit to the Nova Exhibition in London?Well, it started before that. A lot of musicians were putting flags onstage and using words that I didn’t necessarily support. I had posted a few positive comments online [supporting Nova survivors], and a couple of artists did the usual “shame on you, shame on you.” And I started to see it was getting a lot of rage online. I [thought], I’ll write about what’s going on, because there’s only so many love songs you can write. I’ve known Jewish people since I was a teenager in London. Being in the fashion world and obviously rock ‘n’ roll, it would be very amazing if you didn’t know someone Jewish.

Recent findings suggest that given that, were you surprised by the lack of compassion for Oct. 7 victims?I think people were very quick to celebrate what happened on October the 7th and change the narrative, twist it around, make it about something else. And it felt that some of the reaction was already planned. As soon as I saw a Palestinian umbrella, I was like, they got products. This isn’t just people with cardboard and some words scratched on it. A lot of musicians I respected were saying ‘Free Palestine.’ And there was no voice for the Jewish community in London. I went to New York and was given an award by [ewish publication] Tablet magazine for my support of the Jewish people, and I felt a little bit like a fraud. But at that point, nobody was saying anything. So I was kind of like a lone wolf in that sense. Did that inform the single?The song really came out of me going to Fresh York, getting this award, and thinking, “I really want to do something measured and powerful.” I almost didn’t go to [to Nova]. I thought it was going to be really traumatic. I grew up not that long after the Second World War. We knew about the Holocaust, and anyone that indicates it’s not true makes me really angry. So when this [Oct. 7 denial] started to happen, I thought to myself, “I never thought I would live in a world where this would happen again, where this language was being used again.” I wasn’t able to not say something. My Jewish friends said to me, “You’re saying things that we can’t say.”.

In a recent development, being an ally can be fraught these days…Sometimes you need allies from outside, like straight guys supporting gay people and trans people. You need allies that are not part of that group. In the Seventies, when we started Culture Club, our whole ethos was about anti-racism and anti-prejudice. All that stuff was really the backbone of what we were singing about, which is why we called ourselves Culture Club, and why we wore the Jewish star and presented Rastafarian images. We probably naively were mixing up a lot of religious ideas, but it was more about that feeling of why can’t people just live in harmony? … My tastes are very eclectic, not only musically but also culturally. As a kid, if I saw a religious Jewish guy, I’d be like, “That look!” I am interested in other people and human beings.

Industry observers note that so, was your iconic hat a nod to the Hasidic look?That hat was an original Hasidic hat, and in fact, when John [Moss, Culture Club drummer and George’s former boyfriend] went to buy it, because my initials are G.O.D., for George O’Dowd, they wouldn’t put that in the hat. It would have been great!

What’s it like performing your old hits now?I feel like it’s an ending of something for me. I’m not saying I’ll never sing those songs again. Of course I will, but my feeling is that next year I might start a very different type of band, a punk band or a reggae band. I just need to do something different, because I feel like that old boy George doesn’t really exist anymore.

Do you mean the insecure 20-something George who dated his bandmate, got into drugs, and went to prison, as depicted in the Culture Club documentary?I was dealing with a very complicated relationship. I’d grown up in a very dysfunctional family, where there was a lot of fighting, and you grow up thinking that that’s normal. I went from one dysfunctional relationship to another, which is why I joke now that creativity is my lover. One thing I’ve learned in the last 10, 15 years is that songwriting is not hard. Finding what you want to say is the biggest challenge. A song like “We Will Dance Again” kind of wrote itself. When I was at Nova, I saw “we will dance again” written everywhere, and I was like, well, there’s the hook! And then the rest of it was simply looking at what was being noted and using those words in a very blatant way, literally reading stuff out of the newspaper and challenging that as a writer, which I think is the job of an artist to say, “Is there another way of looking at this?” I’ve never said anything negative about Palestine, or anywhere else. It’s about me saying, “I know my Jewish friends are good people. I know this to be a fact.” They fed me more than any other race. You want to be my friend? Feed me.

Recent findings suggest that so touring Israel was less of a political stance than a humanitarian one for you?I don’t really have a stance. I don’t even know what that means. I’ve been called everything you can think of: Goy George, Genocide George, all of that stuff. I felt like I had to go, and now that I’m back in London, it was the right thing to do. I will go back and do a recording of the songs that I did at Menorah [Mivtachim Arena], because it would be great to put it out as a Boy George in Israel tribute. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With several acclaimed roles under his belt, Mahershala Ali still finds himself on equal footing in many casting rooms.

The 2x Academy Award winner recently explained that having the Oscar statuettes “doesn’t matter” in casting conversations, explaining that the coveted acting honor is “kind of just talk” and “doesn’t translate to anything real.”.

Industry observers note that “It’s a natural way for people to think. But on some level, what does an Oscar mean? It’s an award, and it’s an award where you’re being recognized, hopefully for doing good work. But there’s a lot of great actors that don’t have Oscars, who are also looking for good material. So, it doesn’t really mean anything. And that’s no disrespect to The Academy or the award at all, but what I’m actually saying is that, Oscar or no Oscar, there’s a lot of good actors out there,” he explained on the 7pm in Brooklyn podcast. “There’s more good actors than there is good material.”.

Sources indicate that ali continued, “And it’s not even that all these people are competing for these same spots. It’s just that out of all the material made, there’s only a handful of them that check certain boxes. And then you got to be right for it. Just because a script is good doesn’t mean that I’m right for it or whoever wrote it is thinking about me, of all people. So, who is centered? The vast majority of projects that get greenlit, there are not roles for me in those. You gotta think that way, you know what I mean? So, it doesn’t matter if I got 17 Oscars. If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you’re like everybody else waiting and looking and searching.” Watch on Deadline.

Noting that rollbacks of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) programs “on some level impact what gets greenlit,” Ali explained “that if certain companies are allowed to not feel a pressure to be reflective of the world we live in, they’ll just keep centering who they see in their offices, and it ain’t a bunch of us in those offices.”.

Sources indicate that at the same time, Ali doesn’t want to be typecast in another “diversity project,” adding, “You just want to do great material as a Black person. You’re not thinking of yourself as this exotic other, per se. You just are living your life. You wake up. You put your pants on like everybody else. You just want to be like, ‘Yo, this is my offering. This is my story. This is my work.’ Opposed to, ‘Man, who are the best Black actors?'”.

With Ali earning Oscar buzz for his latest starring role in Bassam Tariq’s Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, the actor previously won Best Supporting Actor for Moonlight in 2017 and Green Book in 2019.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a week of controversy, Russell Brand’s wife promised to no longer share her husband’s statements from prison.

In the latest episode in the couple’s Sunday Service series — now hosted solely by Laura Brand, with some prerecorded footage of her now-imprisoned husband — Laura told viewers, “Last week’s episode drew a considerable amount of attention and, now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant staff at HMP Littlehey [prison], I will absolutely honor that.”.

In the video posted last Sunday following Russell’s conviction and sentencing, Laura read a message to listeners from Russell where he reiterated, “I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”.

That communique sparked a firestorm in the U.K., where “prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances,” a spokesperson for the prime minister stated.

The Prison Service of England and Wales requested that the Google-owned YouTube take down the video, saying Brand’s message was “distressing for victims.” However, Google denied the request, stating that — while hurtful for the victims — Brand’s video didn’t violate any of the platform’s rules. Industry observers note that according to the Daily Mail, Laura Brand visited her husband this week at HMP Littlehey, where she also met with prison officials. It’s unclear what was discussed, but on Sunday Laura remarked she would refrain from spreading future messages from Russell, instead continuing “to be proud to be a wife, and a mother, and a woman defending her family at a time when the media’s image of what kind of a woman I am is under so much scrutiny.”.

Russell Brand was sentenced to over 10 years in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault. On Saturday, his wellness brand Reborn started selling shirts with the message “Free Russell” on them.

Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a fresh filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the manufacturer complies.
  • As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.
  • Industry observers note that apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a fresh filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the manufacturer complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Industry observers note that apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a new filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its latest filing, Epic says Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the manufacturer of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

According to recent reports, apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple states decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s newly introduced CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”.

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

According to recent reports, under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

In a recent development, given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”.

According to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a new order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.
